seoTitle: How to Integrate Google Sheets with Google Tasks
metaDescription: Push rows from Google Sheets into your Google Tasks sidebar automatically using Apps Script, so tracking spreadsheets become an actionable to-do list.
intro: Copying tasks manually from a tracking spreadsheet into your Google Tasks list is tedious and easy to forget. A lightweight Google Apps Script can push your task titles, due dates, and notes straight from Sheets into your Tasks sidebar. This guide walks through the setup.

steps.heading: Structure your spreadsheet columns
steps.body: Set up dedicated columns for task titles, due dates, and notes to prepare for the integration.

steps.heading: Format dates correctly
steps.body: Make sure dates and times are formatted properly so Google Tasks registers them correctly.

steps.heading: Open the Apps Script editor
steps.body: Access the built-in Google Apps Script editor from your spreadsheet's Extensions menu.

steps.heading: Paste and modify the script
steps.body: Add the lightweight script code and adjust it to match your specific target task list.

steps.heading: Authorize account permissions
steps.body: Grant the required account access securely so the script can create tasks on your behalf.

steps.heading: Run the live sync
steps.body: Execute the script to push your spreadsheet rows into Google Tasks and confirm they appear correctly.

faq.question: Do I need to write the script myself?
faq.answer: No, the process involves pasting a lightweight script and modifying a few details, like your target task list, rather than writing one from scratch.

faq.question: Will this create duplicate tasks if I run it more than once?
faq.answer: This depends on how the script is written; it's worth reviewing the logic or adding safeguards if you plan to run the sync repeatedly on the same rows.

faq.question: What data does the script transfer?
faq.answer: Typically task titles, due dates, and notes are mapped from your spreadsheet columns into corresponding Google Tasks fields.

faq.question: Is this safe to run on a shared spreadsheet?
faq.answer: The script requires you to authorize account permissions, so it's best to review exactly what access it requests before running it on a shared file.
